steps.title: Crush sediment sample
steps.instruction: Place the bag containing the sediment into a mortar, keep a small air pocket inside, and use a pestle to crush the sample as finely as possible.

steps.title: Collect ground powder
steps.instruction: Pour the ground powder through a funnel into sealable Falcon test tubes for storage.

steps.title: Load centrifuge tubes
steps.instruction: Transfer the powder into 2.0 mL centrifuge tubes, filling each tube to one‑third of its height (≈0.5 mL sediment per tube).

steps.title: Prepare 30 % HCl solution
steps.instruction: In a covered fume hood, pour 50 mL of 30 % hydrochloric acid (HCl) into a small beaker while wearing gloves, lab coat, and safety goggles.

steps.title: Add acid to tubes
steps.instruction: Carefully pipet a small amount of the 30 % HCl into each centrifuge tube, stir gently with a clean pipet, and keep an ice bath nearby to control any exothermic reaction.

steps.title: Fill tubes with acid
steps.instruction: Pipet additional 30 % HCl to each tube, leaving enough headspace to close the cap; add slowly to avoid bubbling over.

steps.title: Allow carbonate reaction to finish
steps.instruction: Wait until bubbling stops; if bubbling is slow, place the tubes on a hot plate and heat to a maximum of 70 °C until bubbling ceases.

steps.title: Centrifuge carbonate reaction
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tubes at 1700 rpm for 10 minutes (00:10:00) to pellet the sediment.

steps.title: Decant supernatant
steps.instruction: Carefully pipet the supernatant into a 1000 mL waste beaker that is half‑filled with water.

steps.title: Rinse with distilled water
steps.instruction: Fill each centrifuge tube with distilled water (dH₂O), remix the sample with a pipet tip to un‑pellet, then repeat the centrifugation (step 7) and decanting (step 8). Perform this rinse until the supernatant is clear, approximately two times.

steps.title: Dispose HCl waste
steps.instruction: Flush the acidic waste down the sink while running cold tap water for 5 minutes (00:05:00).

steps.title: Dry sample with acetone
steps.instruction: Repeat step 9 using acetone instead of water; pipet the acetone supernatant into a 100 mL waste beaker, then place the tubes and the waste beaker in a fume hood to evaporate for 1–2 days. After 3 days, wash the now‑empty beaker.

steps.title: Prepare 30 % H₂O₂ solution
steps.instruction: If organics are present, fill each centrifuge tube halfway with 30 % hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂) in a covered fume hood while wearing appropriate PPE.

steps.title: Initial peroxide heating
steps.instruction: Place the tubes on a hot plate and warm to 40 °C; if the reaction becomes vigorous, remove from heat and place the tubes in an ice bucket until the reaction ceases.

steps.title: Increase peroxide temperature
steps.instruction: After 30–60 minutes (00:30:00–01:00:00), raise the temperature to 80 °C. If the reaction is minimal or absent, raise to 100 °C. Stir gently with a pipet tip every 5 minutes. Continue until no visible reaction occurs, then proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Fill tubes with peroxide
steps.instruction: Completely fill the centrifuge tubes with 30 % H₂O₂, observing the colour change from black → red/brown → orange → clear yellow/green as organics are destroyed.

steps.title: Extended peroxide treatment
steps.instruction: If the reaction has not ceased within 8 hours, leave the tubes on the hot plate overnight at 80 °C; top off with fresh 30 % H₂O₂ the next morning if evaporation occurred.

steps.title: Cool and centrifuge
steps.instruction: When the solution becomes a clear yellow or yellow/green, remove tubes from heat, allow them to cool, then centrifuge at 1700 rpm for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Remove peroxide and rinse
steps.instruction: Pipet off the supernatant, rinse the pellet with water, and dry the sample by repeating step 11 (acetone rinse and evaporation).

steps.title: Prepare ZnBr₂ stock solution
steps.instruction: In a beaker on a magnetic stirrer, slowly add 500 g solid zinc bromide (ZnBr₂) to 175 mL distilled water; the exothermic reaction will generate heat.

steps.title: Make 2.3 g/mL ZnBr₂ solution
steps.instruction: To obtain a density of 2.3 g/mL, mix 250 g ZnBr₂ with 87.36 mL distilled water, then verify the density with a hydrometer (target 2.30 ± 0.057 g/mL). Adjust by adding water (if density too high) or ZnBr₂ (if density too low) until within range.

steps.title: Store ZnBr₂ solution
steps.instruction: Pour the verified solution into a glass bottle, cap it, and label with the preparation date and measured density.

steps.title: Set up flotation tubes
steps.instruction: Prepare a new set of labeled centrifuge tubes and pipets with bulbs; add the dried sediment sample to each tube.

steps.title: Add ZnBr₂ flotation medium
steps.instruction: Fill each tube with the ZnBr₂ solution, leaving enough headspace to close the cap.

steps.title: Collect surface microfossils
steps.instruction: Using a fresh pipet, draw off the microfossil‑rich surface layer into a new labeled test tube. If no material is visible, still draw 0.5–1 mL from near the tube wall, focusing on the ring of floating particles.

steps.title: Dilute and centrifuge flotation
steps.instruction: Fill a clear wash bottle with hot non‑distilled water, add water to the tube to dilute the ZnBr₂‑microfossil mixture, stir with a pipet, then centrifuge at 1700 rpm for 10 minutes and decant the supernatant into a designated ‘Waste ZnBr₂’ container (do not pour down the sink).

steps.title: Repeat flotation if needed
steps.instruction: If no floated material is observed, top off the original tube with additional ZnBr₂ solution and repeat steps 24–29. Perform the decanting step (step 29) two more times.

steps.title: Acetone wash microfossils
steps.instruction: Wash the collected microfossils using the same water‑rinse, centrifuge, and acetone‑drying procedure described in step 11.

steps.title: Prepare microscope slide
steps.instruction: Label a glass slide and place a drop of immersion oil on it.

steps.title: Transfer powder to slide
steps.instruction: Using a clean spatula, add approximately a quarter of a pinky‑fingernail of the dried powder (from step 32) onto the oil drop.

steps.title: Mix sample on slide
steps.instruction: Mix the oil and powder with the tip of a new glass pipet.

steps.title: Mount coverslip
steps.instruction: Place a coverslip gently on the oil‑sample mixture, first touching an edge then lowering it, and press lightly to create a flat layer of microfossils.

steps.title: Seal slide (optional)
steps.instruction: If the slide will be stored, seal the coverslip edges with clear nail polish, allowing the polish to seep by capillary action.

steps.title: Air‑dry slide
steps.instruction: Leave the slide to air‑dry for at least 24 hours before handling; repeat steps 37 and 37.1 if a better seal is desired.

steps.title: Microscope observation
steps.instruction: Examine the slide with a bright‑field compound microscope (binocular or trinocular). Use a polarizing lens if available. Begin at 40× magnification for overview, then switch to 100× for detailed identification and photography.

steps.title: Collect sediment block
steps.instruction: In a dust‑collector or fume hood with a protective surface (e.g., aluminum foil), outline and chisel out a section of the sediment block for study.

steps.title: Expose stratigraphic layers
steps.instruction: Clean the exposed face of the block so that individual stratigraphic layers are visible.

steps.title: Determine sampling thickness
steps.instruction: Decide the thickness of the sub‑sample based on layer thickness; for densely layered specimens (e.g., varves) use thinner sections to improve temporal resolution.

steps.title: Separate sub‑sample
steps.instruction: Use a flat chisel or similar flat tool to separate a sub‑sample of approximately 0.5 cm depth from the block.

steps.title: Mass sub‑sample
steps.instruction: Weigh the sub‑sample, aiming for consistent mass across all sub‑samples (e.g., ~0.5 g for diatomite) with an accuracy of ±0.05 g.

steps.title: Repeat block preparation
steps.instruction: Repeat steps 1.2–1.4 (crushing, powder collection, loading tubes) for each sub‑sample, cleaning tools and using fresh aluminum foil between samples to avoid cross‑contamination.

steps.title: Bag sub‑samples
steps.instruction: Transfer each sub‑sample into a new plastic sealable bag, then place that bag into a second new plastic sealable bag.
